transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, work has been difficult lately. I manage health services, and anything that takes, you know, real sitting-down brain work—like the monthly reports or trying to plan a multi-site event—it just feels like I hit a wall. I just keep putting it off. Even when I know it matters.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much pleasure or interest from things you usually enjoy, like hobbies, time with family, or other activities?
No... not really. Things outside of work are fine. I haven't noticed a change there.
Do you ever feel down or struggle with motivation outside of work situations, or does it seem to only happen when you're dealing with job-related stress?
No, I don't think so. I don't really feel down. Um... it's just the job. When I'm off the clock, things are fine.
When you're dealing with these job-related tasks, do you find yourself feeling excessively worried or anxious about them, even when you're not actively working on them?
No, not really. I mean, I know the work is piling up, but I'm not sitting around worrying about it. I just... don't do it.
When you're avoiding these job-related tasks, do you feel like it's because you're overwhelmed by them or feel like you won't be able to do them well enough?
No, it's not that. I know how to do my job. It's not about being overwhelmed or... worrying about doing it perfectly. I just... don't get started on it.
Outside of work, do you ever find yourself struggling to stay focused on tasks like reading, following through on plans, or remembering details in your daily routine?
Um... no, not really. I don't read much anyway, so... I haven't noticed anything like that. My routine at home is fine.
Do you ever find yourself losing track of time or forgetting small things during the day, like appointments or where you put your keys, even when it's not related to work?

I suppose. Um... sometimes I forget to return calls from volunteers. Or I'll miss a small errand for an event. Once or twice I've had to apologize because a community meeting just... completely slipped my mind until someone texted me about it. So... yeah. Just things like that.
Do you often find yourself distracted or having trouble staying focused during conversations, even when you're not at work?

Um... I don't know about outside of work. But at work, in meetings... yeah. Like if we're going over a budget update or something, I try to listen, but... if a phone vibrates, or someone's talking out in the hall... I just lose it. Or even if I just think about something I forgot to do for the community league... I'll realize I just missed the last few minutes of what was said. So... yes, I guess.
Looking back, did you have similar issues with staying focused or avoiding tasks when you were a child, like in school or completing chores?

I suppose. Um... yeah, even back in elementary school. My teachers used to tell my parents I was... bright, but always daydreaming. I guess I lost worksheets a lot. And, um... I'd forget to turn in my homework. My mother actually had to check my backpack every night just to make sure it got handed in. So... yeah. I guess so.
Do you often find yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble staying seated, especially in situations where you're expected to sit still?
Um... no. Not really. I don't... I don't really have a problem sitting still. I can stay in my chair fine. It's just... my mind wanders, I guess. But I'm not... bouncing around or anything.
